info.title: Hookwitness API
info.summary: Catch webhooks, script the answers, read the verdicts.
info.description: JSON under <admin prefix>/api/v1 (/admin/api/v1 by default), with the UI's access rules: it answers on IP addresses, localhost and -admin-hosts names (a request with a valid token on any name); writes must be application/json. Once a user exists (or a machine token is configured) every route needs credentials: a personal token as Authorization: Bearer hkw_…, or the web UI's login cookie. Without users the API is open. Every error has one shape (Error). See docs/api.md for recipes.

patch.summary: Change an endpoint's path or turn it on or off
patch.description: Give `path`, `enabled` or both; both change together or, on an error, neither. A new path is validated as the UI validates one; its requests and behaviour stay. Turning an endpoint off keeps everything it has; requests to its path are then answered 404 and kept in the Unmatched register.

post.summary: Draft a JSON Schema from requests
post.description: Drafts a 2020-12 schema from the bodies of the given requests of this endpoint (at most 100): their types, properties (required when in every body; additional ones allowed), arrays' items, integer when every number is whole, null in the type list, a format only when every string has it. Nothing is stored: save it with PUT behaviour (schemas), and map it in a discriminator check if you want.

get.description: The setup file of the endpoints named by `id` (repeat it for several), or of every endpoint. It names each secret and its kind, never a value, hash or fingerprint. Saved as is, it is the file `POST /setup` takes.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: An endpoint to export; absent: all of them.

200.description: The setup file; Content-Disposition names it `<path>.hookwitness.json`.

post.summary: Import endpoints from a setup file
post.description: Creates the file's endpoints, all of them or none. Their secrets are created without values (`set: false`). With `on_conflict=replace` an endpoint already at a path gets the file's behaviour; its requests, counter and on/off state stay, and each secret of the same name and kind keeps its value. Importing the same file again changes nothing.

parameters.name: on_conflict
parameters.description: What to do with a path that is already an endpoint.

201.description: Imported; at least one endpoint was created.

200.description: Imported; existing endpoints replaced or unchanged.

409.description: A path is already an endpoint and `on_conflict` is not `replace` (`duplicate_path`); nothing was imported.

422.description: Not a setup file, a newer format, an unknown field, an invalid path or behaviour (`invalid_setup`); the message names the problem and nothing was imported.

post.summary: Send a caught request again to a URL
post.description: Sends the body's bytes unchanged and the header lines in the order and case they arrived (Host replaced by the target's unless host is received), over HTTP/1.1, without following redirects, and records the answer. The target failing (refused, timeout, reset, TLS) is still a replay, with error set. Targets are checked on the address dialled: link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are always refused, and -replay-allow can narrow them or turn replay off. At most 4 replays run at once.

201.description: The replay, with the answer body.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON or has unknown fields (`bad_json`, `unknown_field`).

409.description: The body was not kept whole, so the request cannot be sent as it arrived (`body_not_kept`).

422.description: A bad input (`invalid`: url, host, timeout_ms), or a target the policy refuses (`target_refused`, field url; the message names the rule).

503.description: Four replays are running, or the bytes held are at -max-inflight (`busy`; try again after Retry-After), or the server is stopping (`stopping`).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: body: each replay carries its answer body.

200.description: The replays; answer bodies only with include=body.

get.summary: Read one replay with the answer body

404.description: No such replay (`not_found`): it went with its request, or newer replays replaced it.

get.summary: The answer body exactly as the target sent it
get.description: With the target's Content-Type, never decompressed, always as an attachment (nosniff, CSP sandbox). At most the first 1 MiB.

code.description: A machine-readable code: not_found, invalid, duplicate_path, stale_version, version_required, conflict, secret_in_use, unknown_field, bad_json, unsupported_media_type, not_an_image, not_kept, too_large, unauthorized, invalid_token, forbidden, session_required, login_off, exists, last_admin, busy, internal.

message.description: What went wrong and what to do, for a person.

field.description: The part of the request at fault: a field (checks[0].secret) or a parameter.

Error.description: The one error shape of every route.

path.description: The exact path senders deliver to.

url.description: Where senders deliver, as reached by this call.

counter.description: Requests that passed its checks since the counter was reset; the rules count these.

enabled.description: On: it catches. Off: it keeps its path, behaviour, secrets, requests and counter, and requests to its path are answered 404 and kept in the Unmatched register.

last_request_at.description: The newest kept request; absent when none.

body_base64.description: The body's exact bytes in base64, sent as they are (not a template); instead of body, for bytes a template cannot say plainly (invalid UTF-8, binary). Giving both is refused. At most 1 MiB decoded.

key.description: A JSON pointer into the body, or a header name.

default.description: For a value with no mapping, or none in the request: one schema, or several (any of). Without it such requests are not checked (n/c).

kind.description: Absent or header: a required header.

header.description: header: the header; hmac: the signature header.

enforce.description: Refuse what does not pass (otherwise only the verdict is recorded).

content.description: hmac: a template of the signed content; the raw body when empty.

schemas.description: schema: instead of schema, several by name; the body must match one of them. The verdict names the one it matched, or, when none did, the closest one with its problems and how many the others had.

text.description: The JSON Schema as a JSON string.

fingerprint.description: A keyed fingerprint; never the value. Empty while the secret is not set.

set.description: False for a secret imported from a setup file whose value has not been given yet: checks that use it give n/v "secret NAME not set" and never refuse. Set it on the secrets route.

standard.description: A whsec_ key, usable by standard checks.

Secret.description: A secret, described: its value is never returned.

secrets.description: Read-only here; set them on the secrets route. Sent back as read, it is ignored.

kind.description: Required for a new secret; a replacement keeps the kind.

status.description: What Hookwitness answered; 0 while a timeout holds it or when nothing was sent.

verdict.description: Overall: fail, else n/v, else pass, else n/c; empty without checks.

body_kept.description: False when the body was over the limit (413) or the server was busy reading other bodies (503).

body_cut.description: True when only the start of the body was kept (the Unmatched register keeps 64 KiB); body_size is the whole.

body_text.description: With include=body: the body when it is UTF-8 text. Absent when the body was not kept.

body_base64.description: With include=body: the body in base64 when it is not UTF-8.

replays.description: How many replays of it are kept (GET /requests/{id}/replays); the newest 50.

path.description: A JSON pointer into the body; empty for the whole body.

not_checked.description: Why the image's pixels were not decoded (it would take too much memory); its header was checked.

Request.description: One request in full: the summary's fields and these.

status.description: What Hookwitness answered; 0 while a timeout holds it or when nothing was sent.

verdict.description: Overall: fail, else n/v, else pass, else n/c; empty without checks.

body_kept.description: False when the body was over the limit (413) or the server was busy reading other bodies (503).

body_cut.description: True when only the start of the body was kept (the Unmatched register keeps 64 KiB); body_size is the whole.

headers.description: As received: order, case and repeats kept; [name, value].

body_text.description: The body when it is UTF-8.

outcome.description: What was done: source (default, rule, check, limit, busy, unmatched — no endpoint at the path, off — the path is an endpoint's that is off), action (reply, timeout, drop, refused, error, abandoned — the sender left during the reply's delay, nothing sent; would_status names the reply it would have got), the reply sent (its body as body, or as body_base64 when it is not UTF-8; cut marks the first 64 KiB; withheld says what of the configured reply HTTP did not send — a body and some headers with 204 or 304, a body to HEAD), delay_ms, waited_ms, counter.

replays.description: How many replays of it are kept (GET /requests/{id}/replays); the newest 50.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 in UTC with exactly three fraction digits, so that times sort and slice as text.

name.description: Suggested: the schema the shared discriminator value maps to, else one from that value (order.paid → OrderPaid), else from the endpoint's path.

exists.description: A schema of that name is stored; saving the draft under that name replaces it.

changes.description: How the draft differs from the stored schema of that name (keys added or not seen, required or optional, types, formats); null when none is stored.

value.description: The value all the requests share; empty when they differ or lack it.

mapped.description: The schema that value maps to now; empty when none.

discriminator.description: The first schema check that picks by a value; null when there is none.

User.description: Someone who may log in. Never the password.

Token.description: A personal token. Its value is in `token` only in the answer that made it.

id.description: The token's public part, for revoking it.

token.description: The value: only when just made, never again.

login.description: false while there are no users (and no machine token): the API is open.

kind.description: key: a signing key; token: a token or password.

SetupSecret.description: A secret the endpoint needs: its name and kind, never a value.

SetupEndpoint.description: One endpoint's setup: its path and behaviour. Requests, counters, the on/off state, ids and times are not part of it.

hookwitness.description: The format marker and version. A file of a newer format is refused.

Setup.description: A setup file: endpoints' behaviour, portable between instances. Unknown fields are refused.

secrets_not_set.description: Secrets of the endpoint without a value: set them on the secrets route.

ReplayIn.description: Where to send the request, and how.

url.description: The target: http or https, with the path and query the request goes to. No user name or password.

host.description: The Host line: the URL's host and port (target), or as caught (received). It keeps its place either way.

insecure_tls.description: https: accept any certificate (self-signed handlers). Recorded with the replay.

timeout_ms.description: The whole exchange; default 30000, at most -max-wait.

Replay.description: A caught request sent again: what was sent where, and what the target answered. status 0 with error set: there was no (complete) answer.

by.description: Who replayed it; empty without login.

line.description: The request line sent: the method, the URL's path and query, HTTP/1.1.

sent.description: The header lines written, in order: the caught ones, with Host as chosen.

notes.description: Where the request sent differs from the one caught (HTTP/1.0 sent as 1.1, a chunked body as one chunk, a Host added).

proto.description: The answer's protocol; empty without an answer.

status.description: The answer's status; 0 without an answer. Redirects are not followed.

headers.description: The answer's header lines as received: order, case and repeats kept.

body_size.description: The answer body's bytes; -1 when it was cut before its end (timeout or reset).

body_cut.description: Only the first 1 MiB (or what arrived) is kept.

duration_ms.description: From the first byte written to the last byte read.

ttfb_ms.description: From the first byte written to the first byte of the answer.

body_text.description: The answer body when it is UTF-8 text, as it arrived (never decompressed). In a list only with include=body.

body_base64.description: The answer body in base64 when it is not UTF-8.

name.name: name
name.description: Letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit.

after.name: after
after.description: Only requests with a larger id, oldest first (0 for the start).

before.name: before
before.description: Only requests with a smaller id (newest first). Not with after.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: At most 500, or 100 with include=body; a larger one is capped.

wait.name: wait
wait.description: With after: wait for a request up to this long (30s, or 30 for seconds; at most 60s).

status.name: status
status.description: Only this answer status; 0 for nothing sent.

from.name: from
from.description: scope=range: RFC 3339, or a local date-time read as UTC.

mask.name: mask
mask.description: Header names whose values are masked; repeat it.

mask_other.name: mask_other
mask_other.description: More header names to mask, comma-separated.

setup.name: setup
setup.description: true adds a section with the endpoint's setup as it is when the report is made: checks, schemas, rules, replies, variables, and secrets by name, kind and whether they are set (never a value).

path.name: path
path.description: A JSON pointer to the image in the body; empty for a body that is an image.

q.name: q
q.description: Only requests whose kept body contains this text: a byte substring, case-sensitive.

json.name: json
json.description: <JSON pointer>=<value>, repeatable, all must match: only requests whose JSON body has at the pointer a string equal to the value, or a number, true, false or null written exactly as the value. The pointer ends at the first =.

include.name: include
include.description: body: each request carries body_text or body_base64, as one request does; limit is then at most 100.

token.name: id
token.description: The token's id (the 8 characters after hkw_).

user.name: name
user.description: The user's name (case does not matter).

bearerAuth.description: A personal token (hkw_<id>_<secret>, from the account page or POST /me/tokens) or the machine token of HOOKWITNESS_API_TOKEN_FILE.

Unauthorized.description: Login is on and the request has no valid credentials (`unauthorized`, `invalid_token`).

Forbidden.description: Not allowed: only an admin manages users and everyone's tokens (`forbidden`); managing tokens and users needs a login, not a token (`session_required`).

Busy.description: Too many password or token checks at once (`busy`); try again after Retry-After.
